Geriatric Nursing

Geriatric nursing — ageing process, common geriatric conditions, falls prevention, elder abuse, end-of-life care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe normal ageing changes
  • Describe common geriatric conditions
  • Explain nursing care for older adults

In simple terms

Geriatric nursing focuses on the care of older adults. As people age, they experience physiological changes and are at higher risk for chronic conditions, falls, cognitive impairment and polypharmacy. Nurses play a key role in promoting healthy ageing, preventing complications and supporting quality of life.

Ageing changes

System Age-related change Clinical implication
Cardiovascular Arterial stiffness, decreased cardiac output Hypertension, orthostatic hypotension
Respiratory Decreased lung elasticity, reduced cough reflex Increased infection risk, impaired clearance
Renal Decreased GFR, reduced concentrating ability Decreased drug clearance, electrolyte imbalance
Musculoskeletal Decreased muscle mass, bone density Falls, fractures, osteoporosis
Neurological Decreased cognitive processing speed Slower reaction time, memory changes
Sensory Decreased vision, hearing, taste, smell Safety risks, malnutrition, social isolation

Common geriatric conditions

Disorder Key signs Nursing care
Delirium Acute confusion, fluctuating consciousness Identify cause, reorient, ensure safety
Dementia Progressive cognitive decline Memory care, safety, support ADLs
Falls Multi-factorial (balance, vision, meds) Fall prevention, environmental assessment
Polypharmacy Multiple medications Medication review, adverse effects
Elder abuse Physical, emotional, financial abuse Recognize signs, report, protect

Nursing care

  • Fall prevention — assess fall risk, assist with mobility, call bell within reach, non-slip footwear, adequate lighting
  • Medication management — medication review, monitor for adverse effects, educate about polypharmacy risks
  • Cognitive assessment — assess cognition, orientation, memory; implement reality orientation techniques
  • Skin integrity — assess skin integrity, prevent pressure ulcers, reposition every 2 hours
  • Nutrition — assess nutritional status, assist with feeding, monitor weight

🔴 Fall prevention

Falls are a leading cause of injury in older adults. Assess fall risk, assist with mobility, call bell within reach, non-slip footwear, adequate lighting, remove hazards.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Fall prevention — assess fall risk, assist with mobility, call bell within reach, non-slip footwear, adequate lighting, remove hazards
  • Medication management — medication review, monitor for adverse effects, educate about polypharmacy risks
  • Cognitive assessment — assess cognition, orientation, memory; implement reality orientation techniques
  • Skin integrity — assess skin integrity, prevent pressure ulcers, reposition every 2 hours
  • Nutrition — assess nutritional status, assist with feeding, monitor weight

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Delirium = acute confusion, fluctuating consciousness; identify cause, reorient, ensure safety.
  2. Dementia = progressive cognitive decline; memory care, safety, support ADLs.
  3. Falls = multi-factorial (balance, vision, meds); fall prevention, environmental assessment.
  4. Polypharmacy = multiple medications; medication review, adverse effects.
  5. Elder abuse = physical, emotional, financial abuse; recognize signs, report, protect.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Delirium = acute onset, fluctuating; dementia = chronic, progressive; distinguish between them.
  2. Falls risk assessment: Morse Fall Scale, Hendrich Fall Risk Model.
  3. Polypharmacy = 5+ medications; increases adverse drug interactions, falls, hospitalisation.
  4. Pressure injury prevention: reposition every 2 hours, assess skin, manage incontinence.
  5. Elder abuse: physical, emotional, financial, sexual abuse, neglect; mandatory reporting.

📌 Memory trick

Geriatric assessment: GERIATRICS — Geriatric assessment, Evaluate function, Review medications, Inquire about falls, Assess cognition, Talk to family, Review safety, Investigate abuse, Consider nutrition, Support independence.

60-second revision

  • Geriatric nursing = care of older adults.
  • Delirium = acute confusion; dementia = progressive cognitive decline.
  • Falls = multi-factorial; fall prevention essential.
  • Polypharmacy = multiple medications; medication review.
  • Elder abuse = physical, emotional, financial abuse; mandatory reporting.

Test yourself

Delirium vs dementia: delirium is:

Answer: B. Delirium = acute onset, fluctuating course; dementia = chronic, progressive decline.

Polypharmacy =

Answer: B. Polypharmacy = typically defined as taking 5 or more medications; increases adverse drug events.

Fall prevention includes:

Answer: B. Fall prevention = assist with mobility, call bell within reach, non-slip footwear, adequate lighting, remove hazards.

Elder abuse includes:

Answer: B. Elder abuse = physical, emotional, sexual, financial abuse and neglect; mandatory reporting.

Pressure ulcer prevention:

Answer: A. Pressure ulcer prevention: reposition every 2 hours, assess skin, maintain skin integrity, adequate nutrition.
